page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.4xlarge is an Arm64-based virtual server instance powered by a 16-core Ampere Altra processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. The instance operates on a KVM hypervisor with dedicated CPU allocation and does not utilize hyperthreading. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the instance delivers average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 28612.3 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9534.0. Memory bandwidth is solid, reaching 1137.11 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 135.55 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1104.0 and a weak bzip3 single-threaded decompression speed of 8.6 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is also a tradeoff, with a weak PassMark CPU encryption score of 2558.55.

Utilizing the Ampere Altra Arm64 architecture provides a cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded workloads due to high physical core density and lower power consumption compared to traditional x86 architectures. This instance is appropriate for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, Redis deployments, and database operations. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or workloads requiring intensive cryptographic operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.4xlarge is an Arm64-based virtual server featuring 16 dedicated Ampere Altra vCPUs clocked at 2.8 GHz and 32.0 GB of system memory. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, this instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. Benchmark results position the server in the average tier for multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and database operations, though it exhibits weaker single-core and cryptographic performance. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it a cost-effective option for scale-out, multi-threaded workloads. It is well-suited for static web serving, containerized microservices, and Redis database deployments.
